steps.body: Eleven, twelve, thirteen — the odd-sounding teens. Their names hide it, but each is still ten and some: 10+1, 10+2, 10+3.
steps.narration: Eleven, twelve, thirteen — the odd-sounding teens. Their names hide it, but each is still ten and some: 10+1, 10+2, 10+3.

widget.prompt: A full group of 10 is already shown. Add the extra dots needed to make 13.

commonCounts.feedback: 0 leaves 3 dots still missing — the ten alone only makes 10, not 13.
2 leaves 1 dot still missing; ten and 2 is 12, one short of 13.
4 adds 1 too many; ten and 4 is 14, one past 13.

widget.missFeedback: The ten is done; count on from 10 while adding dots, and stop when you reach 13.
widget.successFeedback: 13 built — one complete ten and 3 more, exactly what the teen numeral says.

predict.prompt: Does “twelve” contain a ten, even though the name hides it?

options.label: No — twelve is its own thing

predict.reveal: The name is old and strange, but the numeral 12 plainly writes one ten and two ones.

cml.actionGoal: Build one complete ten, then count on the ones, for knb 11 13.
invariants: Every teen number is one complete ten and some ones — the left digit records the finished ten, the right digit counts the extras — and that split is what knb 11 13 rests on.
misconceptions: Reading the 1 of a teen as “one” instead of one TEN, or counting only the leftover ones and forgetting the completed ten.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more dot joined the ones, which teen would the frame show then?

widget.prompt: A group shows 11 dots. Which numeral names that amount?

options.feedback: Correct — a full ten and 1 more is what the numeral 11 says: 1 ten, 1 one.
That numeral names one more dot than the group shows.
That numeral stops one dot short; the ten plus the extra reaches 11.
1 counts only the extra and forgets the whole completed ten underneath.

widget.prompt: What does the numeral 13 secretly say?

options.label: One complete ten, and three more
options.feedback: Correct — the 1 stands for a whole ten, the 3 for the ones riding on top.

options.label: A one and a three, side by side
options.feedback: That reads the digits as neighbours; the left digit is a whole TEN, not a one.

options.label: Three tens and a one
options.feedback: That swaps the digits' jobs — the ten is on the left, the ones on the right.

options.label: Thirteen separate tens
options.feedback: Only the single left digit counts tens; thirteen has exactly one of them.

widget.prompt: What number comes right before 18? Hop one back and tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 18 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop back to reach 17.
16 goes one complete hop too far. Count exactly 1 hop back from 18 to reach 17.

widget.missFeedback: Count 1 back from 18: you land on 17.
widget.successFeedback: 17 — one hop back through the teens, one less than 18.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — one hop back from 18 reaches 17.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — right before 18 means a single hop back, stopping on 17.
